svg.text: Zero-Bubble Pipeline Parallelism: Decoupling Backward Passes
Splitting standard backward B into activation gradient BA and weight gradient BW (Qi et al., ICLR 2024).
Standard 1F1B Backward (Monolithic):
Standard B = BA + BW (Monolithic)
Computes both activation and parameter gradients together
• Critical path blocked: Previous stage waits for full B.
• Parameter gradients BW do not need to be sent upstream.
• Forces idle pipeline bubbles during warmup and drain.
Zero-Bubble Decoupling:
BA (Activation Grad)
Sends dL/dX upstream
BW (Weight Grad)
Postponed to bubble slots
• Fast path: BA unblocks the upstream stage immediately.
• Bubble filling: Deferred BW runs when stage would be idle.
• Eliminates up to 90%+ of the pipeline bubble.
Why Decoupling Works:
• In backpropagation, BA evaluates dL/dX = dL/dY · W^T (needed immediately by stage k − 1 to continue backprop).
• Weight gradient BW evaluates dL/dW = (dL/dY)^T · X (needed only by the local optimizer step at the end of the batch).
• Memory trade-off: Holding forward activations X until postponed BW executes requires a modest 15–25% extra memory.
